text.p: Abraxas Petroleum Corp said Monday it has completed the third well in a seven- well program in Wyoming and three additional wells in the Abraxas Cherry Canyon Field in west Texas.

The company said the Siberia Ridge 4-22 well in Sweetwater County, Wyoming, was dually completed in the Lewis and Almond Sands below 10,700 feet and tested at a combined rate of 410 barrels of oil and 4.6 million cubic feet of natural gas per day after fracture stimulation of both formations.
Abraxas owns a 78.75 percent working interest in the well and the balance is owned by Amoco Corp, Williams Cos Inc and Union Pacific Resources Group Inc.

Abraxas said it is now completing the Siberia Ridge 4-24 well and drilling the Siberia Ridge 5-24 well at a depth of 6,700 feet. The company owns a 75.0 percent working interest in the 4-24 and 5-24 wells together with the same industry partners.
It said the Caprito 83-6 in Ward County, Texas, was completed in the Cherry Canyon "K" and "N" Sands from 6,168 to 6,479 feet.

Following fracture stimulation, the well flowed up the casing 385 barrels of oil and 1.2 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the two sands and 48 barrels of oil and 1.3 million cubic feet of natural gas from the Cherry Canyon "P" Sand.

The company said the Bell Canyon "A" Sand is structurally the highest in the field and has 34 of net pay. The Cherry Canyon "K", "N" and "P" sands will be downhole co-mingled and then dually completed with the Bell Canyon "A" Sand. Abraxas owns an 80 percent working interest in the well.

The Caprito 83-7 in Ward County, Texas, was dually completed in the co-mingled Cherry Canyon and Brushy Canyon Sands together with the Bell Canyon Sand. Following fracture stimulation, the lower zone tested at a rate of 120 barrels of oil and 2.5 million cubic feet of natural gas per day, and the upper zone was fractured and is on gas lift producing 343 barrels of oil and 436,000 cubic feet of natural gas per day. Abraxas owns a 100 percent working interest in the well.

The Caprito 98-8 in Ward County, Texas, was re-completed in the Cherry Canyon "N", "O" and "P" Sands between 6,524 and 6,771 feet. Following fracture stimulation, the well flowed 319 barrels of oil and 705,000 cubic feet of natural gas daily. Abraxas owns a 67 percent working interest in the well.
The company said it intends to drill 23 additional wells in the Abraxas Cherry Canyon Field and 10 additional wells in the Block-16 Cherry Canyon Field during the balance of 1997.
